properties.description: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood (2019), written and directed by Quentin Tarantino and starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, and Margot Robbie, is a comedy-drama set in Los Angeles in 1969. The film is an episodic, character-driven meditation on fame, friendship, obsolescence, and the nostalgic mythmaking of Hollywood, delivered with Tarantino’s trademark mix of sharp dialogue and sudden violence.
properties.plot_summary: In the summer of 1969 Los Angeles, aging TV actor Rick Dalton and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth navigate a changing Hollywood as Dalton’s career falters and Booth drifts between jobs and rumors. properties.description: The Irishman (2019), directed by Martin Scorsese and adapted from Charles Brandt's book I Heard You Paint Houses, is a sprawling biographical crime drama starring Robert De Niro, Al Pacino and Joe Pesci. It follows Frank Sheeran from postwar life into his role as an enforcer for the Bufalino crime family and his alleged involvement in Jimmy Hoffa’s disappearance, told through time-jumping flashbacks and an older narrator. The film is an elegiac, character-driven epic that meditates on loyalty, aging, memory, and the moral cost of violence.
properties.plot_summary: The film traces the life of Frank Sheeran, a WWII veteran who rises from truck driver to mob enforcer for the Bufalino crime family and reflects on his alleged role in Jimmy Hoffa’s disappearance. Told through a series of time-spanning flashbacks and an older Sheeran's recollections, the narrative charts his navigation of loyalty, violence, and the corrosive costs of criminal allegiance. Over decades, relationships fracture and remorse accumulates, leaving a solitary, haunted figure confronting the consequences of his choices.

properties.description: Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance) (2014), directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, is a darkly comic drama starring Michael Keaton, Edward Norton and Zach Galifianakis. The film follows a former superhero movie star who writes, directs and stars in a Broadway play as he confronts fame, ego, and a destabilizing inner voice. Stylistically notable for its long-take illusion, jazz-driven rhythm and backstage setting, the movie explores themes of artistic integrity, identity, and the porous line between reality and performance while mixing satire with psychological intensity.
properties.plot_summary: A once-famous movie star best known for playing a superhero struggles to reclaim relevance by writing, directing, and starring in a new Broadway play. As opening night approaches he battles crippling self-doubt, public scrutiny, and a powerful inner voice that manifests as his former on-screen persona. The production’s tense backstage world exposes rivalries, fragile relationships, and the blurring of performance and reality. The film moves between darkly comic satire and surreal psychological episodes as the protagonist pursues artistic validation at great personal cost.

properties.description: Nocturnal Animals (2016), directed by Tom Ford and starring Amy Adams, Jake Gyllenhaal and Michael Shannon, is a stylish drama-thriller adapted from Austin Wright's novel. The film follows a gallery owner who receives a manuscript from her ex-husband and becomes obsessed with its violent tale, which begins to reflect and unearth regrets from their past. Through its alternating narratives the movie explores revenge, guilt, memory, and the moral consequences of past choices, all rendered in a highly artful, color‑conscious visual style. The result is a tense, unsettling meditation on love, cruelty, and retribution.
properties.plot_summary: A wealthy art gallery owner receives a manuscript from her ex-husband and becomes consumed by the violent novel he has written. As she reads, the book's harrowing tale of a road attack and its aftermath begins to mirror and unearth regrets, memories, and moral failures from their shared past. The film alternates between the protagonist's elegant present life and the brutal story within the book, using the nested narrative to explore revenge, guilt, and the cost of choices. Tension builds as the fictional crime forces confrontations with culpability, grief, and the desire for retribution.
